## `app.api.crowd`

Source: [`backend/app/api/crowd.py`](../backend/app/api/crowd.py)

Routes for student crowd reports (not busy / moderate / crowded).

Calls services.crowd; no aggregation logic lives here. The current level for
every location is also in GET /locations and /locations/{id} (`crowd`).

```python

```

_No description yet._

### `report_crowd`

```python
@router.post('/{location_id}', response_model=Crowd, status_code=201)
def report_crowd(location_id: int, report: CrowdReportIn, request: Request, db: Session=Depends(get_db), throttle: Throttle=Depends(get_throttle))
```

Report how busy a location is right now. Returns the location's crowd level after it.

One report per location per client every CROWD_REPORT_COOLDOWN_SECONDS (429 otherwise).

## `app.api.filters`

Source: [`backend/app/api/filters.py`](../backend/app/api/filters.py)

Routes for dietary filtering, single person and group.

Calls services.filter_engine; no filtering logic lives here. Profiles come in
the request body (POST) so dietary information never lands in URLs or logs,
and nothing about them is stored. One profile is the single-person case.

### `filter_menus`

```python
@router.post('/locations/{location_id}/menus', response_model=list[FilteredMenu])
def filter_menus(location_id: int, request: FilterRequest, on: date | None=Query(None, alias='date'), db: Session=Depends(get_db))
```

Every menu at a location on `date` (default today), each item checked against every profile.

### `filter_group`

```python
@router.post('/group', response_model=list[GroupLocation])
def filter_group(request: FilterRequest, at: datetime | None=None, db: Session=Depends(get_db))
```

Every location, ranked for a group: where everyone has something that fits on `at`'s day.

Order: locations where everyone fits first, then those open at `at`, then by name.

## `app.services.crowd`

Source: [`backend/app/services/crowd.py`](../backend/app/services/crowd.py)

Crowd aggregation.

Combines recent student reports into a crowd level per location.
Kept separate from filter_engine so the two features don't share a file.

Reports are only stored, never updated; the level is worked out here on
every read, so two students reporting at once can't corrupt it. Only reports
from the last CROWD_WINDOW_MINUTES count, and newer ones count more: a report
weighs 1 when new and falls linearly to 0 at the end of the window. No
reports in the window means the level is unknown (None), not "not busy".

### class `Crowd`

_No description yet._

Fields:

- `level: str | None`
- `report_count: int`
- `last_reported_at: datetime | None`

### `aggregate`

```python
def aggregate(reports, at: datetime) -> Crowd
```

reports: (level, created_at) pairs for one location. Only those in (at - WINDOW, at] count.

### class `Throttle`

At most one report per key (client address + location) every `seconds`.

Kept in memory only, so no reporter data is stored. The API is a single
process, so one dict is enough; it resets on restart.

#### `hit`

```python
def hit(self, key) -> float
```

Record a report for key. Returns 0 if allowed, else seconds until it would be.

## `app.services.filter_engine`

Source: [`backend/app/services/filter_engine.py`](../backend/app/services/filter_engine.py)

```text
Dietary filter engine.

Checks menu items against one or more dietary profiles and labels each
result as fits, conflicts, or incomplete (data incomplete). Never treats
missing allergen data as safe. Pure functions, no database.

The rules, per profile (a wrong "fits" can hurt someone, so every gap in the
data makes a result incomplete, never fits):

Allergens the profile avoids
    the item lists one (icon, or its label's "Contains:")   conflicts
    the item has a trait or "Contains:" name we don't know  incomplete: it might be one
    the item has no nutrition label                         incomplete: icons alone may miss one
Diets the profile requires
    the item is tagged with it (vegan also counts as vegetarian)        fits
    the item lists an allergen the diet rules out (DIET_EXCLUDES)       conflicts
    otherwise                                                           incomplete: untagged
                                                                        doesn't prove either way
Goals (min protein, max calories, max sodium)
    no label, or the label doesn't give that nutrient       incomplete
    outside the limit                                       conflicts

Overall: any conflict -> conflicts, else any incomplete -> incomplete, else fits.
```

### class `Profile`

_No description yet._

Fields:

- `avoid: frozenset[str]`
- `diets: frozenset[str]`
- `min_protein_g: float | None`
- `max_calories: float | None`
- `max_sodium_mg: float | None`

## `app.services.hours`

Source: [`backend/app/services/hours.py`](../backend/app/services/hours.py)

Opening hours: turn stored hours rows into times, and answer "open at T?".

Pure functions, no database. Ingestion stores one row per location and date
(db.models.HoursDay): status "open" / "closed" / "unknown", and windows as
[open_minute, close_minute] after that date's midnight. A close at or past
1440 runs into the next day, so "open at 12:30am" must also check the
previous day's row.

### `campus_time`

```python
def campus_time(at: datetime | None=None) -> datetime
```

`at` in campus time. None means now; a naive datetime is taken as campus time.

### `periods`

```python
def periods(day: date, windows: list) -> list[tuple[datetime, datetime]]
```

[[420, 1260]] on 2026-10-06 -> [(Oct 6 7:00am, Oct 6 9:00pm)], in campus time.

Hours for one location on one date, from dining.ncsu.edu. Writer: ingestion.

past 1440 means the location closes at or after midnight.

One nutrition label. Writer: ingestion.

Scoped per location because two halls can serve different recipes under one name.

### class `MenuItem` (Base)

One dish on one menu. Writer: ingestion (replaced wholesale on each scrape).

allergens = the item's icon traits plus its label's "Contains:" list.
unrecognized_traits holds any icon or "Contains:" name we have no key for; the
filter engine must treat a non-empty list as "data incomplete", not as safe.
nutrition_key is NULL when no label was fetched or it failed verification.

Fields:

- `id: Mapped[int]`
- `menu_id: Mapped[int]`
- `detail_oid: Mapped[int]`
- `name: Mapped[str]`
- `course: Mapped[str | None]`
- `serving_size: Mapped[str | None]`
- `traits_raw: Mapped[list]`
- `allergens: Mapped[list]`
- `diets: Mapped[list]`
- `unrecognized_traits: Mapped[list]`
- `nutrition_key: Mapped[str | None]`
- `menu: Mapped[Menu]`
- `nutrition: Mapped[Nutrition | None]`

### class `IngestRun` (Base)

One run of the ingestion job: status, options, stats, errors. Writer: ingestion.

The API can read the latest row to show how fresh the data is.

Fields:

- `id: Mapped[int]`
- `started_at: Mapped[datetime]`

## `ingestion.fetch`

Source: [`ingestion/fetch.py`](../ingestion/fetch.py)

```text
Fetch: the only code that talks to the network.

Polite by design: one request at a time, at least REQUEST_DELAY_SECONDS apart,
an identifying User-Agent, and backed-off retries only for errors worth retrying.

NetNutrition is stateful. The first GET sets an ASP.NET session cookie, and every
click after that is a POST to <page>/<Controller>/<Action> (see the site's own
Scripts/cbord_nn_ui_repsonsive.js) answering
    {"success": true, "panels": [{"id": "menuPanel", "html": "..."}, ...]}
The server remembers the selected unit and menu, so calls must run in order:
select unit -> select menu -> labels for that menu. Never parallelize a session.
```

# M0 eval: `eval/`

## `eval`

Source: [`eval/__init__.py`](../eval/__init__.py)

M0 risk-killer eval (see docs/m0-eval.md).

The eval runs PackPlate's real filter engine, which lives in backend/app, so
backend/ goes on the import path here. That keeps the one command,
`python -m eval.m0` from proj_2/, working without extra setup.

## `eval.baseline`

Source: [`eval/baseline.py`](../eval/baseline.py)

The icon-only baseline M0 compares PackPlate against.

It filters the way NetNutrition's own trait filter does: it reads only the
icons on the menu. Avoiding an allergen, an item is out only if it shows that
allergen's icon; no icon counts as safe, even with no nutrition label, an
"Unknown" trait, or the allergen listed only in the label's "Contains:" line.
Requiring a diet, an item fits only if it carries that diet's icon, with the
same rule as PackPlate (vegan also counts as vegetarian), so the comparison
isolates how missing allergen data is handled.

There is no "incomplete": every answer is fits or conflicts.

### `check`

```python
def check(icons: list[str], profile: Profile) -> str
```

One item, given its icon titles as published, against one profile.

## `eval.m0`

Source: [`eval/m0.py`](../eval/m0.py)

```text
M0 risk-killer eval: is PackPlate safe, and is it useful? One command, from proj_2/:

    python -m eval.m0            # compute, print, and write eval/results.json
    python -m eval.m0 --check    # recompute and fail if it differs from results.json

Inputs, all committed: the frozen snapshot, the hand spot-check sheet, and the
simulation settings. Thresholds were posted in the pre-registration issue
before the first run. A missed threshold is reported, not an error: only a
crash, a stale spot-check sheet, or (with --check) a changed result fails.

Safe: every `fits` answer was scanned against its ingredient list; a person
read every flag (and 30 random unflagged answers). Confirmed flags are false
fits, counted separately for PackPlate and the icon-only baseline.

Useful: a simulated group is answered if some location is open at the group's
time and every person has at least one `fits` item on that meal's menu (or an
all-day menu). Unknown hours count as closed: we can't promise it's open.
```

## `eval.scan`

Source: [`eval/scan.py`](../eval/scan.py)

```text
Ingredient scan: does an item's ingredient text name something a profile avoids?

This is M0's independent safety check. PackPlate's filter never reads
ingredient text (it uses the icons and the label's "Contains:" line), so a
`fits` item whose ingredients name an avoided allergen is a lead worth a
human look. The words are in eval/wordlist.py.

Two kinds of hit are kept apart:
- `terms`: words in the ingredients themselves.
- `advisory`: words only inside a cross-contact warning ("may contain",
  "made in a facility that also processes ..."). Those aren't ingredients,
  so they're reported separately, not counted as false fits.
```

## `eval.spot_check`

Source: [`eval/spot_check.py`](../eval/spot_check.py)

```text
Build the hand spot-check sheet: every scan flag, plus 30 random unflagged items.

Run once, from proj_2/:

    python -m eval.spot_check

It writes eval/data/spot_check.csv for a person to fill in, and refuses to
overwrite a sheet that already exists, so filled-in decisions can't be lost.

One row per recipe (nutrition label) per test profile: the same dish on many
menus is read once. Only items that come out `fits` under PackPlate or the
icon-only baseline are scanned, since only those can be false fits.

The `decision` column:
- flagged rows: "confirm" (a real false fit) or "reject" (the word misfired)
- sample rows: "ok" (nothing avoided in the ingredients) or "missed" (the scan
  missed something)
```

## `eval.wordlist`

Source: [`eval/wordlist.py`](../eval/wordlist.py)

```text
Ingredient words that mean an item breaks a test profile. Reviewed by a human.

For each test profile: `terms` that flag an item, and `except_` phrases that are
removed before matching because they look like a term but aren't one (cocoa
butter isn't dairy). Matching ignores case, needs whole words, and also matches
a plural "s" / "es". A flag is only a lead: a person confirms or rejects every
one in the spot-check.

Deliberately left out, and listed as limits in the results:
- "natural flavors", "spices", "seasoning": can hide an allergen, but the text
  doesn't say which.
- coconut: not counted as a nut here; NC State's "Contains Nuts" covers peanuts
  and tree nuts and doesn't say how it treats coconut.
- oats: often contaminated with gluten, but not a gluten ingredient.
- vanilla extract and other flavor extracts: contain alcohol, but whether that
  matters for halal is disputed.
- Meat that isn't pork can't be shown to be non-halal from ingredients.
```
